headline: Giménez returns: Atletico clear favourites against winless Deportivo
summary: Atletico Madrid's six-game winning run ended in Stuttgart on Tuesday, 1-1, with a red card and four days to recover. Deportivo La Coruna arrive with eight days' rest but no win in five league games. Atletico are second in La Liga on 22 points. José María Giménez, more than a decade at Atletico, returns as a Deportivo centre-back; Mundo Deportivo report he asked for no clause stopping him playing. Across 10 bookmakers, margin removed, Atletico are 74.3% favourites, and on the handicap Deportivo get a head start of 1.75 goals. The goals total has come down from 3.07 to 2.97, so the market sees control, not a rout.
read: Atletico Madrid are strong 74% favourites at home to a Deportivo side without a win in five, with the handicap set at -1.75 and the goals line at 3.0. The subplot is José María Giménez coming back to the Metropolitano with Deportivo, days after Atletico's six-game winning run ended with a 10-man 1-1 in Stuttgart.

facts.fact: Atletico Madrid are 74.3% to win at home — more than seven times Deportivo's 9.4% chance.
facts.meaning: The market treats this as a strongly one-sided game, with the draw (16.4%) the only other outcome given real weight.

facts.fact: Atletico are second in La Liga with 22 points from nine games — seven wins, one draw, one defeat and a +11 goal difference.
facts.meaning: That league record is the base under their price: only one defeat in nine and the best part of a two-goal-per-game cushion.

facts.fact: Atletico's six-match winning run ended on Tuesday with a 1-1 Champions League draw at Stuttgart, where they finished the game with 10 men.
José María Giménez, now a Deportivo centre-back, faces Atletico — the club he spent more than a decade at — for the first time, and said he asked that no fear clause be included.
facts.meaning: Deportivo's back line will be organised around a defender who knows Atletico's forwards better than anyone on the pitch.

facts.fact: Deportivo have not won in five La Liga games — DLDLD, three draws and two defeats.
facts.meaning: They arrive rested but winless, which is why the market gives them under a tenth of a chance.

facts.fact: Deportivo have averaged 1.27 xG across their last five games, scoring five goals from it.
facts.meaning: They create enough to be a counter-attacking threat even while the results stay flat.

facts.fact: Atletico have won four of the last five meetings between the clubs, and none of the five produced more than two goals.
facts.meaning: Recent history points to a narrow Atletico win rather than a high-scoring one.

facts.fact: The handicap line is Atletico -1.75, with the fair line at -1.67 — the market rates them roughly 1.7 goals the better side.
facts.meaning: The price asks Atletico to win by two goals or more before the line pays out in full.

sources.fact: Atletico Madrid's six-game winning run ended with a 1-1 Champions League draw at Stuttgart, during which they played with 10 men after a red card.
Julian Alvarez scored his first goal of the season for Atletico in the draw at Stuttgart.
Alex Grimaldo said of Alvarez after the Stuttgart draw: "Julian is our best player. He's been creating chances for a few games now and he needed that goal."
An Atletico defender is reported to miss the Deportivo La Coruna game at the Metropolitano but is expected back a week later at Valencia.
Atletico Madrid sit second in the LaLiga table, behind leaders Barcelona.
Jose Maria Gimenez, now a Deportivo central defender, will face Atletico Madrid, his club of more than a decade, for the first time; he said he asked that no fear clause be included.
Gimenez acknowledged that his time at Atletico Madrid is over.
Deportivo La Coruna go to the Metropolitano looking to spring a surprise at one of LaLiga's most demanding venues, in a match billed as a classic-style occasion.
